original_value: The goal of this article is to provide a thorough introduction to the state of the art in magnetic methods for remote-manipulation and wireless-actuation tasks in robotics. The article synthesizes prior works using a unified notation, enabling straightforward application in robotics. It begins with a discussion of the magnetic fields generated by magnetic materials and electromagnets, how magnetic materials become magnetized in an applied field, and the forces and torques generated on magnetic objects. It then describes systems used to generate and control applied magnetic fields, including both electromagnetic and permanent-magnet systems. Finally, it surveys work from a variety of robotic application areas in which researchers have utilized magnetic methods, including microrobotics, medical robotics, haptics, and aerospace.

result.paraphrase: This article aims to give a comprehensive overview of the current state of the art in magnetic techniques for remote manipulation and wireless actuation in robotics. It brings together previous work under a unified notation to make application in robotics easier. The discussion starts with magnetic fields produced by magnetic materials and electromagnets, explains how magnetic materials become magnetized in an applied field, and covers the forces and torques acting on magnetic objects. It then outlines systems for generating and controlling applied magnetic fields, including electromagnetic and permanent-magnet systems. Lastly, it reviews research across several robotic application areas where magnetic methods have been used, such as microrobotics, medical robotics, haptics, and aerospace.
